title: Invertibility of a tensor-pullback adjunction unit on an isomorphism locus
statement: Let p:X\to Y be a morphism of schemes and U an open subscheme of Y [def-pc-scheme]. Suppose the projection X\times_Y U\to U is an isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let adj be any adjunction p^*\dashv p_* for the tensor pullback and module pushforward [def-pc-module-pullback]. For every sheaf A of O_Y-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the restriction to U of the unit A\to p_*p^*A is an isomorphism. No properness, Noetherianity or coherence hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proof, adjunction morphism on the complement; sectionwise proof using source-library Modules.PullbackUnit

proof.text: Use the standard pullback unit. For j:U to Y, let g and q be the two projections of X times_Y U. g is an open immersion and q is an isomorphism. For a section-open V contained in U, p inverse V is contained in the range of g. The unit of g is bijective there. The composite g followed by p equals q followed by j, an open immersion with range U, so its unit is bijective on V. The source-library pullbackUnit_comp_app identifies its unit, up to the invertible pullbackComp map, with the unit of p followed by that of g. Cancel the latter bijection to show that the unit of p is bijective on V. Componentwise bijectivity proves invertibility after restriction.

Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq relates the standard pullback adjunction to the given tensor adjunction. Its unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app formula writes the supplied unit as the standard unit followed by pushforward of an isomorphism. Restriction preserves this isomorphism, so the result applies to every supplied adjunction.

theorem tensorPullback_unit_restriction_isIso
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Y) (U : Y.Opens)
    (hp : IsIso (pullback.snd p U.ι))
    (adj : tensorPullback p ⊣ pushforward p) (A : Y.Modules) :
    IsIso ((restrictFunctor U.ι).map (adj.unit.app A))
